Hot 3.0.2 keeps secrets out of call records in more of the places they could appear, and adds `::hot::ctx/mark-secret` for credentials passed as arguments.

## Security

- **Secrets inside longer strings are now masked in call and run records.** Masking used to compare whole values, so a secret composed into a longer string, such as a `Bearer` header or a form body, was recorded as it was. A registered secret is now masked wherever it appears inside a string, raw, URL-encoded, JSON-escaped, base64-encoded or as a quoted CSV cell holds it. Values shorter than 8 bytes are still masked only as whole values.
- **Credential fields are masked whether or not anything marked them as secret:** `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `X-Api-Key` and similar headers, and fields like `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `client_secret`, `password` and `api_key`, in Maps, JSON and form bodies, and returned values.
- **`::hot::ctx/set-secret`, and `::hot::ctx/set` of a declared secret key, now mask their own call records** and register the value at once, instead of at the first `::hot::ctx/get`.
- **Webhook and MCP requests:** the fields the API marked as sensitive, including `secret-headers`, now reach the worker. They weren't reaching it before.
- **Call errors, and failures on run and env streams, are masked.**
- **Bytes are masked in every form a record holds them.** A secret inside `Bytes` was masked in the value but not in a failure's message, which renders it as `Bytes([83, 69, ...])`. So a run ending in an `Err` holding a response's `body-bytes` could record it in `run.result` and `alert.data`. Rendered bytes, and Vecs holding only bytes, are now checked like Bytes themselves, for registered secrets and credential fields. Streams mask Bytes holding a registered secret, and `hot run` masks an `Err` it prints as a result.
- **Records already written:** a secret a run registers now masks the call rows it has already written, whether those calls are still running or finished. It happens right away the first time, at most every 30 seconds for a run that keeps registering new ones, and once more when the run ends. Values already spilled to blob storage aren't masked again.
- **Keys and signatures:** the key or password given to `::hot::hmac/*`, `::hot::crypto/rsa-sha256-sign` and `::hot::crypto/pbkdf2-hmac-sha256`, and what they return, as itself or in hex or base64, are masked without anything marking them. A token signed during a run could be rebuilt from the signature and its encoding in the call records.

If you ran API calls with Bearer or Basic auth on an earlier version, see the upgrade guide: records written then may hold those credentials.

## New

- **hot-std:** `::hot::ctx/mark-secret(value)` masks a value in this run's records without storing it in the context, and returns it. Packages that depend on it need `hot-min-version: "3.0.2"`.
- **hot-std:** `::hot::csv` reads and writes CSV and TSV: `from-csv`, `to-csv`, `from-tsv` and `to-tsv`. Values stay `Str` unless the `types` option converts them, so ZIP codes and IDs keep their leading zeros. Malformed input is an Err naming the line. Packages that depend on it need `hot-min-version: "3.0.2"`.
- **hot-std:** `iter-csv` and `iter-tsv` read rows one at a time, and `::hot::file/read-file-stream` reads a file as an iterator of chunks without loading it. Together they read files too big for memory, and keep rows out of call records when the callback is a lambda. `from-csv` records the rows it returns, so prefer `iter-csv` for large files or personal data.

## Fixes

- **An arrow now runs for its own target and source, not a same-named one in another namespace.** When two namespaces, such as two API packages, each declared `HttpError` and `HttpResponse -> HttpError`, the last one loaded ran for both, so `HttpError(response)` could return the other package's type and skip this package's redaction. The same applied to implicit coercion at a parameter, and a value could run the arrow of a same-named source type.
- **A parameter whose type is written qualified or through a namespace alias now gets its implicit arrow.** `x: ::api/Error` and `x: ::alias/Error` passed `hot check`, but the function received the value unconverted. They now behave like `x: Error`.

## Behaviour changes

- **A parameter annotated with a built-in type now rejects other values at the call.** `"443"` or `443.5` reaching `x: Int` through an `Any` value, such as a field of parsed JSON, returns `Err(ConstraintError.Violation)` naming the parameter and function, instead of failing later as `mul requires numbers` or not at all. Null fails too, unless the annotation allows it (`x: Int?`). An `Int` becomes a `Dec` at `x: Dec`, and a whole `Dec` such as `443.0` becomes an `Int` at `x: Int`. `Vec<T>` and `Map<K, V>` check the container only; user types, `Any` and `Fn` aren't checked. If your code passes values its annotations don't allow, widen the annotation or convert the value. A failed check is an `Err`, and `if` treats an `Err` as false, so a condition can take its false branch rather than halt. See [Parameter Checks](https://hot.dev/docs/language/types#parameter-checks).
- Overloads with a rest parameter now dispatch on their arguments, in both tiers. `concat` used to run an overload chosen by position, whichever types it was given.
- `::hot::str/length`, `is-empty` and `slice` are no longer core functions, so bare `length`, `is-empty` and `slice` always reach `::hot::coll`, which also takes null at `is-empty` and iterators at `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `some`, `all` and `find-first`.
- `::ai::agent::runtime/now-epoch-secs` in `hot-ai-agent` returns whole seconds, as its `Int` annotation says. It returned a fractional `Dec`, so new notification store keys no longer hold fractional seconds.
- Responses from `::hot::http/request`, `get`, `post` and the other request and streaming functions, `::hot::file` metadata, and `::hot::box/stats` and `allowed-images` now carry their declared type. `T(response)` runs a declared `HttpResponse -> T` arrow instead of copying fields. Field access is unchanged, but `is-map(response)` is now `false` and `to-json(response)` gives tagged JSON. Use `untype(response)` for a plain Map.
- HMACs and signatures read `<secret>` in stored call records and run results, including an HMAC a program computes to show. The program still gets the real value.
- A stored `run.result` no longer holds credential fields or registered secrets: code that reads a run's result back through the API sees `<secret>` for them. A webhook or MCP caller waiting on the run still receives the real result.
- `true`, `false`, `null` and `""` are no longer masked just because a secret Map contains them.
- A key's declared `default` isn't masked inside longer strings. It is still masked as a whole value unless the key is `secret: false`.

See [Secret Masking](https://hot.dev/docs/language/meta#secret-masking) for what is and isn't covered.
